title: Targeted Transcript Profiling of Ecdysone-, Juvenile Hormone-, Bursicon- and Cuticle-Related Genes in Drone Pupae and Adults of the Honey Bee Apis mellifera: An RT-qPCR Study
content: Background: Honey bee drones are haploid males whose quality shapes the reproductive success of queens, yet the molecular events that accompany their pupa-to-adult transition have not been characterised. In workers this transition is paced by the decline of ecdysteroids and involves ecdysone-signalling, juvenile hormone (JH)-pathway, bursicon-pathway and cuticle-formation genes. Methods: Total RNA was extracted from pooled drone pupae (n = 3) and pooled newly emerged adult drones (n = 3), reverse-transcribed, and analysed by SYBR Green RT-qPCR on a QuantStudio 5. Eleven target genes (EcR, Usp, BR-C, Kr-h1, Burs α, rk, Amlac2, AmelCPR14, AmelTwdl1, AmelTwdl2, Ampxd) were profiled and amplicons were examined by agarose gel electrophoresis. Relative abundance was expressed as the log2 ratio of Ct values (adult/pupa), and again after median-centring of the panel. Results: RNA was pure and intact (A260/A280 = 2.0; A260/A230 = 2.1), and all 11 target genes amplified in both stages across a wide abundance range (Ct 15.4–29.8). Ten of 11 genes were higher in the adult. The largest increases were for Kr-h1 (+3.91 log2 units; about 15-fold), AmelTwdl2 (+3.22), Usp (+2.78) and Burs α (+1.89), whereas EcR was the only gene higher in the pupa (−1.11). BR-C and Ampxd were nearly unchanged. The ranking of genes was identical after median-centring. Discrete amplicons were confirmed in both stages for EcR, Amlac2 and AmelCPR14, and in the adult for Usp, Kr-h1 and rk. Conclusions: This is the drone-specific RT-qPCR profile of hormone-responsive, bursicon-pathway and cuticle genes across the pupa-to-adult transition. It reveals a coordinated, adult-biased programme in which a fall in EcR is accompanied by a rise in Usp and Kr-h1, in the bursicon pathway (Burs α, rk) and in cuticle effector genes (AmelTwdl2, Amlac2, AmelCPR14), in line with the logic established in workers. Kr-h1, Usp, Burs α and AmelTwdl2 emerge as candidate molecular markers of drone adult maturation.
